bullets.title: NVDA: ATH test, Hugging Face acquisition, OpenAI Astra GPU demand, $2.5B Thinking Machines consideration
bullets.body: NVDA tests all-time highs alongside AAPL, driving MAG7 +2.4%; the company is reportedly considering acquiring Hugging Face (~$150M run-rate revenue) to anchor the open-source AI stack and drive broader compute demand. OpenAI's Astra trained on 100K NVDA GPUs and OpenAI CTO confirms ongoing reliance on Nvidia for cutting-edge capabilities; US model release cadence hit 12.5/quarter in Q3 (vs 7.4 in Q2), one of 11 factors in a 97% R² model for NVDA datacenter revenue. NVDA also guided +70% Y/Y FY28 revenue growth per JPM, with supply constraints remaining; separately considering a $2.5B investment in Thinking Machines Lab (ex-OpenAI CTO Mira Murati).

bullets.title: ADBE: CEO transition to Anil Chakravarthy signals enterprise CX pivot; stock -3.9% pre-market
bullets.body: Adobe named Anil Chakravarthy as next CEO succeeding Shantanu Narayen (effective Dec 1), with David Wadhwani departing. The market read is a strategic shift toward CX and enterprise workflows while Creative remains under pressure from AI competition (Figma/Canva). Stock was -3.9% in pre-market; Citi flagged OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra as a watch item for ADBE given its capabilities in design automation.

bullets.title: TTD: 15% RIF (~576 roles) saves $86-115M annually; Citi maintains Sell at $11 PT (-27% downside)
bullets.body: Trade Desk announced ~15% workforce reduction in 3Q26, generating estimated $86-115M in annualized savings with $39-51M in restructuring charges. Citi maintains Sell/High Risk with $11 PT (5x '27E EV/EBITDA on $765M EBITDA), arguing new products (Measurement, Audience Unlimited, Zuma) and go-to-market revamp need several quarters to drive durable growth; 3Q26 EBITDA margin guided at 24.6%, down 1,830bps Y/Y vs. a 40%+ long-term target. TTD traded +2.2% in pre-market despite the news.

bullets.title: CDNS/SNPS: Down 5-7% on OpenAI GPT-6 Astra PCB layout demo automating EDA workflow
bullets.body: SNPS -7% and CDNS -5% despite SOXX +3% after OpenAI released a video of GPT-6 Astra performing PCB layout design in KiCad — a manual task described as a common source of latency in electronics design. Market concern is that AI automation threatens the EDA software bottleneck these vendors monetize.

bullets.title: AVGO: Anthropic scaling to 30GW compute by 2030; AVGO XPUs ramp to 70%+ of fleet by decade-end
bullets.body: Broadcom's conference call confirmed 5GW/10GW demand from Anthropic in 2027/2028, with AVGO XPUs ramping to 70%+ of Anthropic's fleet by end of decade (vs. NVDA peaking at ~30% in 2027). Anthropic currently targeting $45B revenue at 2GW capacity and $200B+ at 7GW scale; AVGO guided AI Revenue to double in FY27 and double again in FY28 per JPM.

bullets.title: TSLA: Cybercab Austin launch underwhelming; -3.4% pre-market, MS sees robotaxi tracker as key catalyst
bullets.body: Tesla officially began public Cybercab rides in Austin but only 45 units have been registered in Texas, with limited availability. Stock was -3.4% pre-market; Morgan Stanley's analyst believes yesterday's outperformance appropriately priced progress and sees publicly available fleet expansion trackers (unsupervised Cybercab + Model Y) as the key next catalyst to watch.

bullets.title: NFLX: Price hikes in Germany/Austria (~18% of EMEA subs); JPM flags EU pricing power
bullets.body: Netflix raised prices in Germany (Standard +€2, Premium +€2, AVOD +€1) and Austria, affecting ~18% of EMEA subscribers (~6% of total); Citi estimates ~4% uplift in EMEA ARPU. UK prices also raised (AVOD +£2, Standard +£1, Premium +£2) per JPM, reinforcing NFLX's global pricing power thesis.

bullets.title: CRWD: Fal.con drives $20B ARR target pulled in one year to CY34; SafeMind agentic AI in limited preview
bullets.body: CrowdStrike reiterated FY28 NNARR growth target of 20%+ Y/Y and pulled forward its $20B ARR target to CY34 (one year earlier than prior guidance). SafeMind agentic AI security system — which autonomously discovers vulnerabilities and remediates — enters limited preview with 2H rollout, sold on token basis through Falcon Flex. Partner checks show no negative feedback; one partner flagged disappointment with SentinelOne's technical performance.

bullets.title: ORCL: Tactically positive into earnings; Cloud AI capacity near 63% YoY growth, GPUaaS GM raised to 19%
bullets.body: MS TMT flags ORCL as tactically positive ahead of earnings: Cloud AI capacity tracking toward 58-64% guide, GPUaaS gross margin raised to 19% (from prior 12%), and channel checks show stabilizing Cloud Apps. Stock was +2.7% in pre-market.

bullets.title: MU: HBM pricing strong but moderating; HBM4 ASP premium >50%, HBM4E to command 25-40% additional premium
bullets.body: Korean customs data shows HBM proxy export value per unit +228% YoY and +10% MoM in July (44% above April levels), indicating strong pricing but moderated peak growth. HBM4 ASP premiums remain >50% on a capacity basis; HBM4E expected to command 25-40% same-capacity premium over HBM4. Rubin (NVDA) and custom ASIC ramp in H2 2026 are cited as major HBM4 demand drivers.

bullets.title: CIEN: Big F3Q26 beat; guides FY27 revenue +30%+ with 45-46% GM; PT trimmed 5% to $605
bullets.body: Ciena reported F3Q26 revenue of $1.67B (+1.8% vs consensus), gross margin 46.4%, and operating margin 22.5%, crushing consensus by ~250bps. FY27 guidance of 'at least' +30% revenue growth with 45-46% GM and 25-27% OPM (vs Street at 22.7%) impressed; direct cloud revenue +80% YoY with market share up 4pts to ~30% in optical. JPM reiterates OW but trims Dec-27 PT to $605 (down 5%).

bullets.title: EQIX/DLR: Citi reiterates Buy on both; models 25% IT Load CAGR to 370 GW by 2031
bullets.body: Citi refreshes its global data center model forecasting IT Load CAGR of 25% from 121 GW in 2026 to 370 GW in 2031, driven by AI/HPC workloads and agentic AI adoption. Citi reiterates Buy on both EQIX and DLR, noting each 100bps upside to 5-year CAGR can be net accretive by ~5%. Equinix also announced Fabric One and Inference Exchange (AI inference) products launching 1Q27.

bullets.title: HOOD: +16.5% yesterday on false Blockworks crypto volume data ($36B amended to ~$2B); JPM expects shares to be offered
bullets.body: Robinhood surged 16.5% on reportedly incorrect Blockworks on-chain spot trading volume data showing $36B notional, subsequently amended to ~$2B. JPM analyst is 'deeply skeptical' of HOOD's risk/reward and expects shares to be offered (sold) this morning as corrected data surfaces. Stock was -4.1% in pre-market.

bullets.title: BKNG/CVNA: Morgan Stanley highlights as non-AI high-conviction OW ideas with idiosyncratic catalysts
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley is hosting a 9/8 webcast on non-AI best ideas featuring BKNG (strong execution through volatile macro with AI optionality), CVNA (OW, $90 PT — near-term reset for long-term flywheel), and WAB (OW, FY26 guidance ahead of consensus, accelerating backlog-driven growth). All three positioned as idiosyncratic earners not dependent on the AI capex cycle.

bullets.title: AFRM/FSLR: JPM specialist sales desk backs both as undervalued with improving fundamentals
bullets.body: JPM Global Specialist Sales is bullish on AFRM (beat-and-raise quarter, mid-30s GMV growth, low-30s revenue growth, Card product flywheel; FY27 guide implies high-20s growth de-risking cycle concerns) and FSLR (de-rated below 9x 2027E earnings post-catalyst; $0.44/watt pricing upside could drive ~$17/share valuation benefit, with recent bookings in mid-$0.30s vs. $0.32 assumed for FY28).

bullets.title: PATH: Hedgeye maintains Top Short; software growth decelerated to 11.2%, FCF conversion near zero
bullets.body: Hedgeye argues PATH's Q2 beat of $12.8M was entirely driven by negative-margin professional services (-86% GM) and upfront licenses, while subscription services (64.9% of revenue) missed by $3.6M. Software revenue growth decelerated 515bps from Q1's +16.4% to Q2's +11.2%; H1 adjusted FCF fell $0.7M despite $49.6M incremental operating income (0% conversion). Contract assets rose 48.4% while deferred revenue fell 13%, widening cash collection gap.

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 Pro starting price $1,249-$1,299 on 400% memory cost surge; foldable build raised to 7-8M units
bullets.body: iPhone 18 Pro is expected to start at $1,249-$1,299 (Pro Max $1,349-$1,399) due to a 400% Y/Y increase in 256GB memory costs. Separately, supply chain checks suggest Apple's foldable build has been raised to 7-8M units for C2H'26 (20M first-gen cycle), with a starting price of $2,399 implying 1.5pts ASP lift per 1% mix shift. iPhone Ultra production was throttled to a few hundred units/day in August due to quality inspection rejections.

bullets.title: PLTR/SNOW/NET: GS Communacopia preview — AI capex-to-revenue translation is the central investor debate
bullets.body: With 260+ companies and 2,000+ investors at GS Communacopia in SF, the central debate is whether $375B+ cumulative AI capex (YE25-YE28) translates to sustainable revenue outside frontier names. Palantir showed 149% US commercial revenue growth; Cloudflare noted rising agentic activity; Snowflake flagged faster AI-enabled migrations in Q2. Key risk: Nvidia profits supported by investor capital through model labs rather than self-sustaining customer economics.

bullets.title: CHTR: CFO Jessica Fischer departing for Google-Blackstone TPU Neocloud, flagging weak turnaround conviction
bullets.body: Charter Communications CFO Jessica Fischer is departing for a Google-Blackstone TPU Neocloud venture, which is being read by analysts as a signal of weak internal conviction in Charter's turnaround narrative.

bullets.title: SHOP/APP/RBLX/ETSY: JPM SMid Internet AMA on Sept 14 to cover best ideas and 2H/2027 catalysts
bullets.body: JPM analyst Bryan Smilek is hosting an Internet SMid 'Ask Me Anything' on September 14, covering RBLX, ETSY, APP, and SHOP as focus stocks. Discussion will include post-coverage-expansion views, management/industry expert takeaways, and best ideas heading into 2H and 2027.
